::::

::: prose
In fall 2024 SPRAWL V2 was used at The Goat Farm Arts Center in Atlanta. Twelve access points were set up, each with a musician playing their own instrument into the system. The concert consisted of student-created programs ranging from real-time spatialised granular synthesis to a graphic score visible to audience and musicians. At the access point shown, the drum is picked up by a microphone into the audio interface and fed into the system; other access points let the audience play along.
:::

## SuperCollider Symposium, DC · Spring 2025

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![Workshop at the SuperCollider Symposium.](pictures/scsymp_workshop.jpg){.photo .ph}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Workshop**

- Techniques for distributed systems
- Fully connected mesh
- Attendees prgrammed, using Ansible

::: {.box .fragment}
**Logistics**

- **5 access points**
- **10-hour drive** in a midsize car


:::
:::
::::

::: prose
After being taught in the classroom in fall 2024, SPRAWL V2 went to Washington, DC in spring 2025 for a workshop at the SuperCollider Symposium. The workshop covered techniques for working with SPRAWL V2 and, more generally, with distributed performance systems; attendees designed the audio processing for their own access point in the mesh. Bringing five access points meant a ten-hour drive from Atlanta in a midsize vehicle. That trip motivated MËSH.
:::
